title: コミュニケーション・デザイン入門
subtitle: Introduction to Communication Design
educationalGoal: This course cultivates the ability to design effective questions that elicit feasible information and create meaningful dialogue. Students will reconstruct ideas from collected data and enhance them through collaboration. They will also develop fundamental skills to clearly communicate ideas to others. Additionally, the course covers methods for creating communication spaces that support smooth observation, as well as techniques for refining and verifying hypotheses derived from observations through lectures and practical exercises.
advice: In this course, students will engage in a project-based learning experience focused on both tangible and intangible creation. The course is structured around four key processes: "Questioning," "Dialogue," "Collaboration," and "Communication." Through these processes, students will design communication spaces within each stage of the project. By doing so, they will come to understand the importance of fundamental communication skills necessary for comprehending and solving social issues. 1) Designing Questions: students will learn how to prepare and structure effective questions that facilitate meaningful discussions when investigating latent needs from stakeholders. 2) Designing Dialogue: students will explore how to create an environment that fosters effective dialogue during field investigations or in simulated settings. 3) Designing Collaboration: students will learn how to define problems as a team based on research findings, formulate hypotheses, and design a collaborative environment to develop concrete solutions. 4) Designing Communication: students will examine how to effectively communicate their project outcomes to stakeholders and design appropriate methods and settings for presentation. Advice for Learning: It is recommended to consciously observe aspects of daily life, such as "easy-to-use objects" and "people in a relaxed state." Additionally, considering the reasons and factors behind these observations is also beneficial for learning in this course.
books: Textbooks:"The Art of Discussion" by Jun Nakahara, published by PHP Institute, 2022. Reference books:"Designing of Questions" by Yuki Anzai and Takayuki Shiose, published by Gakugei Publishing, 2020. Reserved books:None specified
requiredKnowledge: No prior preparation is required. However, there are many excellent books on communication that cover a wide range of topics, from improving individual skills to facilitating team activities. Reading such books as reference materials is recommended. Additional recommended readings will be introduced during the lectures as needed.
